reader.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un made an unannounced visit to China, crossing a newly inaugurated cross-border bridge into Dandong, signalling a warming of bilateral trade and military ties. A magnitude-7 earthquake struck Tibet, killing 16 people, injuring 76, and collapsing hundreds of homes. China's Q3 GDP grew 4.5 percent, beating forecasts, driven by a strong AI export boom that offset domestic consumption weakness. The US banned Chinese AI startup DeepSeek from government agency systems, prompting Beijing to object and DeepSeek to raise 15 billion dollars ahead of a potential IPO. Xi Jinping convened the Communist Party's fifth plenum, emphasising discipline among top cadres, while a long-serving political figure was reported to have fallen from grace. China's stock market slid deeper into bear territory as AI-related shares shed 150 billion dollars in value. Volvo Cars plunged 24 percent after its CEO declared the Chinese market effectively lost to Western automakers. Citi received long-awaited approval to open a wholly owned securities unit in Beijing. Taiwan reported driving away 16 Chinese vessels it described as part of a 'hybrid warfare' campaign. Typhoon Champi approached the Chinese coast after battering Taiwan and Japan.

China's stock market slid deeper into bear territory as AI-related shares lost 150 billion dollars in value over a 10-week rout.
Volvo Cars shares plunged 24 percent after its CEO said the Chinese market was effectively gone for Western automakers.
Citi won long-awaited regulatory approval to open a wholly owned securities company in China after nearly a five-year wait.
Taiwan reported driving away 16 Chinese vessels it said were part of a 'hybrid warfare' maritime harassment campaign.
Trump said he was open to a trilateral meeting with Putin and Xi, and the Kremlin confirmed China was preparing for the possible summit.

plain.summary: Over the coming week, the dominant story will be the Communist Party's fifth plenum, which convenes this week and will produce a formal policy communiqué setting economic and industrial priorities, with a strong emphasis on AI self-sufficiency and cadre discipline. In the background, rescue operations in Tibet will draw to a close as the government announces a reconstruction plan for earthquake-affected communities. The US-China AI rift will sharpen: Beijing will lodge a formal protest over the DeepSeek ban, and the startup will push forward with its IPO preparations. The stock market will stay under pressure, and a surprise monetary easing from the central bank is a realistic possibility. The typhoon will pass, and the Kim Jong Un visit will give way to follow-up diplomatic coverage. Overall, the week will be defined by the plenum's output and the escalating tech rivalry with Washington.

Beijing will respond to the US exclusion of DeepSeek from government systems with formal countermeasures targeting American AI firms operating in China, escalating the tech standoff. display.eli5:
China is in the middle of a big AI fight with the United States. The US government banned a Chinese AI company called DeepSeek from using its systems, and Beijing is angry. Next week, China will probably announce its own rules to push back, making the tech rivalry even hotter.

At the same time, China's Communist Party is holding a big meeting called the fifth plenum. This is where top leaders decide policy and sometimes fire or move powerful officials. We should expect to see more news about who got kicked out and what economic plans they announced.

In the mountains of Tibet, a big earthquake shook the ground and killed at least 16 people. Rescuers are still digging through collapsed buildings. The death toll will probably go up as they reach remote villages, and the government will likely declare an emergency.

A real surprise would be if the US, Russia, and China all agree to sit down together at a summit in China to talk about the Ukraine war. That would be a major shift in world politics.
